title: Ending a Ridgecrest RxSecure Enrollment and Withdrawing an Application
content:
Only the member, or a representative they have appointed in writing, may end a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan enrollment or withdraw an application; a pharmacy, a prescriber or a relative may never end it for them.

A request to end the drug plan is recorded on the enrollment intake as a voluntary disenrollment, standing as recorded, as awaiting the member's signature, or as submitted to CMS, before the enrollment is ended.

## The two ways an enrollment comes to an end

**A voluntary disenrollment** takes effect on the last day of the month in which the plan received the request, and the member keeps drug coverage until that day.

**An application withdrawn before the coverage effective date** leaves no coverage period at all: the enrollment is cancelled before it became effective, the disenrollment reason recorded is that it was withdrawn before the effective date, and any premium already paid is refunded in full.

## What the member is told

The plan tells a member ending their drug coverage outside an election period that they may not be able to join another plan until the next annual election period, and that months without creditable coverage will count toward a future late enrollment penalty.

Ending the drug plan does not by itself end any medical plan the member holds, and a member who meant to end both is asked plainly which they want ended.
